premises.text: People buy brand clothes because they want to talk about them and show others what they have and wear
premises.evidence_span: They want to talk about them. They want others get to know what they have, what they wear

premises.text: People often see clothing they want but cannot identify the brand or where to buy it
premises.evidence_span: you see somebody, for example, in a cafe wearing with gorgeous shoes, and you realize you want the same one

premises.text: Brand-in tags let users label brands on their own photos and on photos from social networks
premises.evidence_span: It provides them with the tools for tagging brands on their photos and even on photos from social networks like Facebook

premises.text: The community answers brand-identification questions through the app
premises.evidence_span: ask community what brand it is by making a question branding

premises.text: Photo polls deliver purchase advice from friends and fashion experts in less than a minute
premises.evidence_span: Take photos of yourself and create a poll. In less than a minute, you'll get a lot of advice

premises.text: The web service brings people together on the basis of their brand loyalty, with wardrobes, wish lists, and cross-site tagging
premises.evidence_span: brings people together on the basis of their brand's loyalty

premises.text: Brands will pay to communicate with their fans and with fans of their competitors
premises.evidence_span: brands can communicate with their fans and even with fans of their competitors

premises.text: A store marketplace automatically attaches purchase links to brand-ins by analyzing store price lists for keywords
premises.evidence_span: Stores provide us with a price list and our system analyze keywords and automatically attach the links to the branding

value.text: Brand-loving people can discover what brand something is and where to buy it
value.evidence_span: how to know what brand it is and where to buy it

secondary_value.text: Brands gain a direct channel to communicate with their own and their competitors' fans
secondary_value.evidence_span: brands can communicate with their fans and even with fans of their competitors

notes: Heavy ASR noise ('TechBrand'/'Tag Brand', 'BookMarket' bookmarklet); corrected silently in premise text where unambiguous. 'Just launched' status, pending app approval, international expansion plans, investment search, and team experience excluded per 4.2. No dependency links coded; none plainly asserted. Partition happens to follow need/features/monetization: justified because community tagging mechanics, the brand-loyalty need claims, and the brand/store monetization modules are separately revisable (monetization could change without altering tagging, and vice versa).
